title: ragnar_find_links() ignores <lastmod> dates in sitemap XML
description:
When `ragnar_find_links()` is called with a sitemap URL (e.g. `"https://docs.posit.co/sitemap.xml"`), the `<lastmod>` elements present in the XML are silently discarded. The `last_modified` attribute on the result is either `NA` for every URL, or (when `get_timestamps = TRUE`) populated by issuing a HEAD request per URL, which is expensive and redundant.

## Expected behaviour

`attr(links, "last_modified")` should be populated directly from the `<lastmod>` values in the sitemap XML, with no HEAD requests needed for URLs that already have a date.

## Actual behaviour

All `last_modified` entries are `NA` unless `get_timestamps = TRUE`, in which case HEAD requests are made for every URL even though the sitemap already contains the information.

## Minimal reproducible example

```r
links <- ragnar_find_links("https://docs.posit.co/sitemap.xml")
attr(links, "last_modified")
# All NA — sitemap <lastmod> values are ignored
```

Inspect the sitemap directly to confirm `<lastmod>` is present:

```r
x <- xml2::read_xml("https://docs.posit.co/sitemap.xml")
xml2::xml_find_all(x, "//*[local-name()='lastmod']") |> xml2::xml_text() |> head()
```

## Root cause

`html_find_links()` extracts only `<loc>` elements from the sitemap `<urlset>`, ignoring sibling `<lastmod>` nodes entirely.

## Fix

Extract `<lastmod>` alongside `<loc>`, parse the dates as `POSIXct` (sitemaps use `YYYY-MM-DD` format), and pre-populate `last_modified` in the crawl loop from those values. URLs whose sitemap entry has no `<lastmod>` fall back to the existing HEAD-request path when `get_timestamps = TRUE`.

title: Add `ragnar_store_audit()` for coverage reporting against an expected URL set
description:
## Problem

After ingesting a large documentation site, there is no built-in way to verify that all expected pages were actually written to the store. Worker errors, network timeouts, and parsing failures can silently drop pages without the pipeline operator knowing.

## Proposed solution

Add a function:

```r
ragnar_store_audit(
  store,
  expected,         # character vector of URLs, data frame, or ragnar_links object
  group_by = NULL   # optional: name of a column in `expected` to group results by
)
```

### `expected` argument

Accepts any of:

- A **character vector** of URLs.
- A **data frame** with a column named `source` (the column name returned by `ragnar_find_links()`).
- A **`ragnar_links` object** (the subclass returned by `ragnar_find_links()`), used directly as a character vector of URLs.

If a data frame is passed, the `source` column provides the URLs and all other columns (including `group_by` columns) are available for grouping.

### `group_by` argument

`group_by` names a column in `expected` (not in the store). The function joins the expected URLs against `documents` on `origin = source`, then groups by the named column. Example: `group_by = "guide"` groups by the `guide` column in the `expected` data frame.

When `group_by = NULL`, the function returns a single-row tibble with no `group` column.

### Return value

A tibble with one row per group (or one row when `group_by = NULL`):

| Column      | Type      | Description                                                   |
|-------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `{group}`   | varies    | Group value (column named after the `group_by` value; absent when `group_by = NULL`) |
| `expected`  | integer   | Number of distinct URLs in the expected set for this group    |
| `ingested`  | integer   | Number of those URLs found in `documents` (distinct origins)  |
| `missing`   | integer   | `expected - ingested`                                         |
| `chunks`    | integer   | Total embedding rows in `embeddings` for ingested pages       |

`ingested` counts distinct origins in `documents` (a UNIQUE constraint on `origin` means at most one row per URL, even after re-ingest).

### Missing URLs

When `missing > 0`, the returned tibble has a list-column `missing_urls` containing the absent URLs for each group. This is the most common follow-up question after seeing a non-zero `missing` count.

## Why ragnar should own this

The workaround joins `ragnar_find_links()` output against `documents` and `embeddings` with raw DuckDB SQL, coupling the caller to ragnar's internal schema. A built-in function remains correct as ragnar evolves its schema.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ragnar_store_audit(store, urls)` accepts a character vector and returns a single-row tibble without a group column.
- `ragnar_store_audit(store, df, group_by = "guide")` returns one row per unique value of `guide` in `df`.
- `ragnar_store_audit(store, ragnar_find_links(...))` works directly on a `ragnar_links` object.
- `ingested` counts distinct origins in `documents`, not chunk counts.
- The returned tibble includes a `missing_urls` list-column containing URLs not found in `documents`.
- The function works on a read-only store connection.

title: Explore using parquet files to utilize pins package for RAG store enable pin_reactive_read as store location
description:
Excellent package. 

In a likely typical usage pattern, users would want to be able to update the store independently from the app upload step to the deployment destination. One potential work around that I am using now is to upload the RAG store duckdb file to a location using the {pins} package. The app downloads the pin at start-up to a temporary location during app run time and this works fine. 

Consider that the RAG store could be pinned to connect, perhaps as a parquet file. Parquet files are already supported for use with the `pins::pin_read`  and `pins::pin_reactive_read` function, allowing a seamless way to have a live connection to the store without the need for uploads or downloads to a temporary file.

The {pins} docs say that `pins::pin_read` returns an R object read from the pin. Would the store location need to be able to support a pins board object as well? 

The use of a parquet file could also prevent issues with concurrent database read/write operations.

The other files supported by `pins::pin_read` are "csv", "json", "rds", "parquet", "arrow", or "qs". It seems like parquet would be the best choice, but these may be other files to consider. Thanks for a great package!

title: Add `ragnar_store_sync()` to remove documents no longer in a crawled URL set
description:
## Problem

When a documentation site is re-crawled, pages removed from the site remain in the ragnar store indefinitely. There is no built-in way to clean them up.

For a production RAG pipeline, stale pages degrade answer quality: the bot may cite URLs that return 404, or retrieve outdated content that contradicts the current docs.

See also #145, which asks this question from a user perspective but has no built-in solution.

## Proposed solution

Add a function:

```r
ragnar_store_sync(
  store,
  urls,                  # character vector of current valid URLs
  filter = NULL,         # optional dplyr-style expression to scope which documents to consider
  rebuild_index = FALSE  # whether to rebuild HNSW/FTS indexes after deletion
)
```

### Scoping with `filter`

Because `guide` is an application-level extra column (not part of ragnar's core schema), the function cannot assume a specific column for scoping. Instead, `filter` accepts a dplyr-style expression evaluated against the `embeddings` table. Example:

```r
ragnar_store_sync(store, urls, filter = guide %in% c("admin-pct", "admin-pwb"))
```

The `filter` expression is evaluated against the `embeddings` table, which includes any extra columns defined at store creation time (e.g. `guide`). It cannot reference `origin` or `text`, which live in the `documents` table. Filtering by document-level attributes (e.g. origin prefix matching) is out of scope for v1.

When `filter = NULL`, the function considers ALL documents in the store whose origin is not in `urls`. This is intentionally conservative: callers doing a partial crawl (e.g. only some guides) must always pass a `filter` to avoid incorrectly deleting documents from uncrawled sections.

### Tables affected

The function deletes consistently from all ragnar-managed tables. In the current schema these are:

- `embeddings`: chunk vectors
- `documents`: source page text and origin
- `page_metadata`: incremental-ingest tracking (if present; ragnar checks before deleting)

If ragnar adds new tables in future, `ragnar_store_sync()` will be updated to include them, so callers are insulated from schema changes.

### Index rebuild

After deletion the HNSW and FTS indexes are stale. The caller controls this via `rebuild_index = FALSE` (default). This mirrors the `build_index` pattern in `ragnar_store_ingest()` and lets callers batch multiple sync operations before a single rebuild.

### Return value

Returns a tibble with one row:

| Column        | Type    | Description                         |
|---------------|---------|-------------------------------------|
| `n_documents` | integer | Number of origin pages removed      |
| `n_chunks`    | integer | Number of embedding rows removed    |

## Why ragnar should own this

The workaround requires raw DuckDB SQL: temp tables, multi-table joins, DELETE statements across `embeddings`, `documents`, and `page_metadata`. This couples the caller to ragnar's internal schema. A built-in function remains correct as ragnar evolves its schema.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ragnar_store_sync(store, urls)` removes all documents whose `origin` is not in `urls`.
- `ragnar_store_sync(store, urls, filter = guide == "admin-pct")` scopes removal to documents matching the filter expression.
- When `filter = NULL`, all documents not in `urls` are considered for removal.
- Deletions are applied consistently to `embeddings`, `documents`, and `page_metadata` (if present).
- `rebuild_index = TRUE` calls `ragnar_store_build_index()` after deletion.
- Returns a tibble with `n_documents` and `n_chunks` removed.

title: ragnar_store_ingest(): support incremental ingest via Last-Modified headers and content hashes
description:
## Problem

Every call to `ragnar_store_ingest()` re-fetches and re-embeds all pages passed in `paths`, even when the remote content has not changed. The internal `prepare_ingest_paths()` (R/ingest.R, line 234) checks whether an origin exists in `documents` and skips re-embedding if so, but it still calls `prepare()`, which fetches and parses the page. There is no mechanism to skip the HTTP fetch.

For large documentation sites (hundreds of pages), this wastes HTTP bandwidth and embedding API budget on every run.

## Proposed solution

Add an `incremental = FALSE` parameter to `ragnar_store_ingest()`. When `TRUE`, ragnar performs a two-tier skip before calling `prepare()`:

**Tier 1: Last-Modified (HTTP URLs only).** Send a conditional `HEAD` request. If the server returns a `Last-Modified` header matching the stored value, skip the page entirely (no fetch, no embed). For local file paths, skip tier 1 and fall through to tier 2.

**Tier 2: Content hash (fallback).** For pages with no usable `Last-Modified` header, fetch the content, compute a hash, and compare against the stored hash. Skip if unchanged.

### Metadata storage

Ragnar manages a `page_metadata` table inside the existing DuckDB store file. The table is created by `ragnar_store_create()` and is always present (empty by default):

```sql
CREATE TABLE page_metadata (
  origin        VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
  last_modified VARCHAR,   -- RFC 2822 string, NULL if not provided by server
  content_hash  VARCHAR    -- rlang::hash() of the markdown content, NULL if tracked by LM
)
```

After each successful ingest, ragnar upserts a row for every origin confirmed written to `documents` (i.e. present in `documents` after the ingest loop completes). Failed pages are not recorded, ensuring they are re-attempted on the next run.

### Dependency note

If #202 (structured return value) is implemented first, "confirmed written" is simply rows where `status == "ok"` in the return tibble. Without #202, ragnar must query `documents` post-loop to identify successful writes.

## Why ragnar should own this

The workaround requires callers to maintain their own `page_metadata` table, implement two-tier skip logic, and re-query `documents` after ingest to confirm writes before recording metadata. This is ~100 lines of boilerplate that every production ingest pipeline needs but must currently write itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ragnar_store_ingest(..., incremental = FALSE)` (default) preserves current behaviour.
- With `incremental = TRUE`, pages whose `Last-Modified` header matches the stored value are skipped without calling `prepare()`.
- For HTTP URLs without a usable `Last-Modified` header, pages are fetched, hashed, and skipped if the hash matches the stored value.
- Local file paths always fall back to content-hash comparison (no `Last-Modified` check).
- `page_metadata` is upserted only for origins confirmed written to `documents`; failed pages are not recorded.
- `ragnar_store_create()` creates the `page_metadata` table as part of normal store initialisation.

title: ragnar_find_links: path-doubling in discovered URLs when following relative links
description:
## Description

When crawling with `depth > 0`, some discovered URLs have their path segment doubled, e.g.:

```
https://docs.posit.co/chronicle/appendix/library/appendix/library/advanced-configuration.html
https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/index.md
```

The first example shows a path repeated (`appendix/library/appendix/library/`). The second shows `.md` source files being discovered as links, which return 404.

## Reproducible example

```r
links <- ragnar_find_links(
  "https://docs.posit.co/reference-architectures.html",
  children_only = TRUE,
  depth = 3
)
# Inspect URLs with doubled path segments
links[grepl("(/.+)\\1", links)]
```

## Suspected cause

Relative links on a page are resolved against the page's URL using `url_absolute()`. If a page's resolved URL already contains a path suffix (e.g. ends in a directory rather than stripping to a base), relative hrefs like `appendix/library/...` get appended to a URL that already contains `appendix/library/`, doubling the segment.

## Impact

- Malformed URLs in the returned vector
- Wasted HEAD requests (all return 404 or connection errors)
- Noise in `last_modified` attribute (all `NA` for these URLs)

title: `ragnar_store_ingest()` should report which paths were successfully written
description:
## Problem

`ragnar_store_ingest()` currently returns the store invisibly (R/ingest.R, line 133) and surfaces worker errors only as warnings (lines 103-109). When a worker fails, the page is absent from `documents` but the caller has no programmatic signal.

This creates a correctness problem for callers recording per-page metadata after ingest (e.g. caching `Last-Modified` timestamps for skip detection). If a failed page's timestamp is recorded, the page is skipped on all future runs, silently losing content from the store.

## Proposed solution

Return the store invisibly as before, but attach a summary tibble as `attr(store, "ingest_summary")`. This is a non-breaking addition: existing callers that pipe or ignore the return value are unaffected, and the summary is available to any caller that asks for it.

```r
result <- ragnar_store_ingest(store, paths, prepare)
summary <- attr(result, "ingest_summary")
```

The summary tibble has one row per input path:

| Column     | Type      | Description                                                      |
|------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `path`     | character | The input URL or file path                                       |
| `status`   | character | One of `"ok"`, `"skipped_exists"`, `"skipped_unchanged"`, `"error"` |
| `n_chunks` | integer   | See below                                                        |
| `message`  | character | Error message for `"error"`; `NA` otherwise                     |

### Status values

- `"ok"`: page was fetched, chunked, embedded, and written to the store.
- `"skipped_exists"`: origin already in `documents`; `prepare()` ran but embedding was skipped (current `prepare_ingest_paths()` behaviour, R/ingest.R line 234). `n_chunks` is the number of chunks already in the store for that origin.
- `"skipped_unchanged"`: page was not fetched because its Last-Modified header or content hash matched the stored value (only possible when `incremental = TRUE`, see #200). `n_chunks` is `0L`.
- `"error"`: worker raised an error; page absent from `documents`. `n_chunks` is `0L`.

### Progress output

The existing `cli_alert_info()` per-page progress (R/ingest.R, line 120) remains unchanged. The structured summary is complementary, not a replacement.

## Why ragnar should own this

The workaround is to re-query `documents` after ingest to find which origins were actually written, then intersect with the input set. This couples the caller to ragnar's schema and adds an extra DB round-trip.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ragnar_store_ingest()` continues to return the store invisibly.
- `attr(result, "ingest_summary")` is a tibble with columns `path`, `status`, `n_chunks`, `message`.
- `status` is one of `"ok"`, `"skipped_exists"`, `"skipped_unchanged"`, `"error"`.
- `n_chunks` for `"skipped_exists"` is the count of chunks already in the store for that origin.
- `n_chunks` for `"skipped_unchanged"` and `"error"` is `0L`.
- `message` is `NA` for non-error rows.
- Existing callers that ignore the return value or pipe the store are unaffected.

title: Worker errors in `ragnar_store_ingest()` are silently swallowed, causing potential data loss
description:
## Problem

In `R/ingest.R` lines 103-108, when a mirai worker raises an error, `ragnar_store_ingest()` catches the condition, re-raises it as a bare `warning()`, and continues the loop with `next`:

```r
if (mirai::is_error_value(result)) {
  # browser()
  cond <- attributes(result)
  class(cond) <- cond$condition.class
  warning(cond)
  next
}
```

The `# browser()` comment on line 104 suggests this was recognised as unfinished during development.

The failed page is absent from `documents` but the caller receives no structured signal. In interactive use, the warning may scroll past unnoticed. In batch or CI use, warnings are often suppressed entirely.

## Why this matters

Any caller that records per-page metadata after ingest (e.g. caching a `Last-Modified` timestamp to skip unchanged pages on future runs) will record metadata for a failed page unless it re-queries `documents` to confirm the write. If the timestamp is recorded, the page is excluded from all future runs, silently and permanently losing content from the store.

This is a correctness bug, not just a usability gap. Even without the `ingest_summary` attribute proposed in #202, the bare `warning()` should carry enough information for a caller to identify which URL failed and why.

## Proposed solution

### 1. Replace bare `warning()` with a structured condition (independent of #202)

Emit a classed condition that carries the failed path and the original error message, so callers can handle it with `withCallingHandlers()` or inspect it programmatically:

```r
rlang::warn(
  message = paste0("Failed to ingest: ", path, "\n", conditionMessage(cond)),
  class   = "ragnar_ingest_worker_error",
  path    = path,
  call    = NULL
)
```

The condition class `ragnar_ingest_worker_error` allows callers to selectively catch worker failures without catching unrelated warnings. Control flow is unchanged: ingest continues past the failure, same as today.

### 2. Remove the `# browser()` comment

This is leftover development scaffolding and should be removed.

### 3. Optional: `max_failures` parameter

Add an optional `max_failures = Inf` parameter to `ragnar_store_ingest()`. `N` counts distinct failed pages (one per path; retries are not currently supported). When the number of failed pages exceeds `max_failures`, ragnar aborts the ingest loop and signals a classed error. Pages successfully written before the threshold is reached are kept in the store (no rollback), consistent with the current "continue past failures" behaviour.

```r
ragnar_store_ingest(store, paths, prepare, max_failures = 10L)
```

## Why ragnar should own this

Callers cannot work around this: there is no public API to enumerate which pages failed, and the bare `warning()` carries no structured data. The only current workaround is to compare `documents` row counts before and after per origin, which is error-prone and schema-coupled.

## Acceptance criteria

### Independent of #202

- Failed worker pages emit a `ragnar_ingest_worker_error` condition (a subclass of `warning`) carrying `path` and the original error message.
- Callers that do not handle `ragnar_ingest_worker_error` see a warning (not an error) and ingest continues, same as today.
- The `# browser()` comment is removed from `R/ingest.R`.
- `max_failures = Inf` (default) preserves current behaviour of continuing past all failures.
- `max_failures = N` aborts after N distinct failed pages with a classed error; pages already written are kept in the store.

### Conditional on #202 landing

- `attr(result, "ingest_summary")` includes `status = "error"` rows for failed pages, with the error message in the `message` column.

title: ragnar_store_ingest() default n_workers formula uses wrong operand order (latent bug, incorrect docstring)
description:
## Problem

In `R/ingest.R` lines 43-46, the default `n_workers` is computed as:

```r
n_workers <-
  max(na.rm = TRUE, parallel::detectCores(), 4L) |>
  min(nrow(paths) %/% 4L, 8) |>
  max(2L)
```

The first call, `max(detectCores(), 4L)`, takes the *larger* of the core count and 4. The docstring (lines 14-15) says the default is "the smaller of `length(paths)` and `parallel::detectCores()`", but the code does the opposite in step one.

### Is this a live or latent bug?

In all current production scenarios the output is correct, because the `min(..., 8)` cap in step 2 masks the over-allocation:

- With >= 32 pages (production): `min(..., nrow(paths) %/% 4L, 8)` clamps to 8 regardless.
- With < 32 pages: `min(..., nrow(paths) %/% 4L)` clamps below 8 regardless.

**This is a latent bug:** the code is wrong in intent, the docstring is wrong, and any future increase to the worker cap would expose incorrect behaviour on high-core machines. It is not currently producing wrong output.

### Concrete example (showing latency)

On a 32-core machine with 40 pages:

```
# Current (wrong intent, correct output by coincidence):
Step 1: max(32, 4) = 32
Step 2: min(32, 40 %/% 4, 8) = min(32, 10, 8) = 8
Step 3: max(8, 2) = 8   <- correct

# If the cap were raised to 16 in future:
Step 2: min(32, 10, 16) = 10   <- correct by coincidence again, but only because nrow cap saves it
```

Reasoning about this formula requires knowing that multiple downstream clamps compensate for the upstream error. Replacing `max()` with `min()` in step 1 makes the intent explicit and the formula self-evident.

## Proposed solution

Replace `max(detectCores(), 4L)` with `min(detectCores(), nrow(paths) %/% 4L)` in the first step, matching the docstring's stated intent ("the smaller of `length(paths)` and `detectCores()`") while retaining the existing `%/% 4L` pages-per-worker throttle and the `min(8L)` cap:

```r
n_workers <-
  min(parallel::detectCores(), nrow(paths) %/% 4L) |>
  min(8L) |>
  max(2L)
```

This is a minimal fix: it corrects the latent bug without changing the pages-per-worker policy. The `%/% 4L` divisor is deliberately retained as a throttle that avoids launching more workers than there are groups of 4 pages to process, keeping daemon startup overhead proportionate to the workload. Removing it would be a separate design decision and is out of scope for this fix.

Update the docstring to match:

> `n_workers`: integer. Number of mirai worker daemons. Default is `max(2, min(detectCores(), nrow(paths) %/% 4L, 8))`: at most 8 workers, at most one worker per 4 pages, at least 2.

## Why ragnar should own this

This is a bug in ragnar's internal default formula. Callers can work around it by always passing `n_workers` explicitly, but the default should be correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- The first step of the `n_workers` formula uses `min(detectCores(), nrow(paths))`.
- The `%/% 4L` divisor in the page-count term is removed; the `min(8L)` cap is retained.
- The docstring for `n_workers` in `?ragnar_store_ingest` matches the corrected formula.
- The `%/% 4L` pages-per-worker throttle is retained unchanged.
- The changelog notes this as a latent bug fix: the formula intent is corrected; output changes only if `detectCores() > 8` and the worker cap is later raised above 8. The pages-per-worker policy is not changed by this fix.
- A test covers the formula for representative combinations of `nrow(paths)` and core counts (testable by mocking `detectCores()`).

title: Allow `ragnar_store_ingest()` to accept a `pre_check` hook for caller-defined skip logic
description:
## Problem

`ragnar_store_ingest()` accepts a `prepare` function but provides no way to skip a URL before `prepare()` runs. Any caller-defined skip decision (e.g. "skip URLs matching a pattern", "skip pages modified before a given date", "skip pages from a blocklist") must be implemented by filtering `paths` before calling `ragnar_store_ingest()`. This works, but gives callers no visibility into skipped pages in the return value (see #202).

Note: for hash-based skip detection specifically, #200 (`incremental = TRUE`) is the preferred solution, where ragnar manages the metadata and skip logic internally. The `pre_check` hook is intended as a general-purpose escape hatch for arbitrary caller-defined conditions that ragnar cannot anticipate.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional `pre_check` parameter to `ragnar_store_ingest()`:

```r
ragnar_store_ingest(
  store,
  paths,
  prepare,
  pre_check = NULL,  # NEW: function(path) -> TRUE (proceed) or FALSE (skip)
  ...
)
```

When provided, `pre_check(path)` is called in the worker before `prepare()`. Returning `FALSE` skips the page without fetching or embedding it.

### Serialisation constraint

`pre_check` is sent to mirai worker processes, the same as `prepare` (R/ingest.R, lines 71-89). It must serialise across the process boundary. **Do not capture a DuckDB connection in the closure**: connections do not serialise and will cause a confusing error in the worker.

Correct pattern: bake any lookup data into the closure at call time.

```r
# Load lookup data in the main process before calling ragnar_store_ingest()
blocklist <- c("https://docs.example.com/legacy/", "https://docs.example.com/draft/")

pre_check <- function(path) {
  !any(startsWith(path, blocklist))  # TRUE = proceed, FALSE = skip
}

ragnar_store_ingest(store, paths, prepare, pre_check = pre_check)
```

Another valid pattern: date-based skip using a named vector baked at call time.

```r
cutoff    <- as.POSIXct("2025-01-01")
page_dates <- setNames(some_files$last_modified, some_files$source)

pre_check <- function(path) {
  d <- page_dates[[path]]
  is.na(d) || d >= cutoff  # skip pages last modified before cutoff
}
```

### Limitation: hash-based `pre_check` does not avoid a double-fetch

If `pre_check` calls `ragnar::read_as_markdown(path)` to compute a content hash, the page is fetched once in `pre_check` and again in `prepare()`, so no bandwidth is saved. For hash-based skip logic, use `incremental = TRUE` (#200) instead, which avoids the double-fetch by passing pre-fetched content through to `prepare()`.

### Return value interaction

When `pre_check(path)` returns `FALSE`, the row in `attr(result, "ingest_summary")` (#202) has `status = "skipped_unchanged"`, indicating the page was not fetched. This reuses `"skipped_unchanged"` because the caller's intent is to assert the page content is known and need not be re-ingested. If the distinction matters, a future revision can add `"skipped_custom"`.

## Why ragnar should own this

Without this hook, a caller with custom skip logic must filter `paths` externally. This gives no structured accounting of skipped pages in the return value, and conflates "never seen before" with "deliberately skipped" in audit output (#203). A `pre_check` hook makes skips explicit and reportable.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ragnar_store_ingest(..., pre_check = NULL)` (default) preserves current behaviour.
- When `pre_check(path)` returns `FALSE`, the page is skipped without calling `prepare()`.
- Skipped pages appear in `attr(result, "ingest_summary")` with `status = "skipped_unchanged"`.
- The documentation includes the serialisation warning and the double-fetch limitation for hash-based implementations.
- At least two non-hash example use cases (e.g. blocklist, date filter) appear in the documentation.

title: ragnar_find_links() does not include the root URL in its results
description:
When you call `ragnar_find_links()` with `depth = 0`, the URL you pass as `x` never appears in the returned vector. Only the links *found on* that page are returned.

```r
ragnar_find_links("https://docs.posit.co", depth = 0, children_only = TRUE)
# Returns 47 child URLs, but not https://docs.posit.co itself
```

This is a bug. The root page is a real, crawlable page at that URL, and there is no good reason to exclude it. Any downstream code that expects a complete list of pages in the tree will silently miss the entry point.

## What is happening

The crawl loop seeds a queue with `start_url` and visits it, but only adds links *discovered on* each page to the `collected` set. The starting URL is never added to `collected`, so it never appears in the output.

## Expected behaviour

`ragnar_find_links("https://docs.posit.co", depth = 0, children_only = TRUE)` should return the root URL as well as its children.

## How raghilda handles this

The Python port [raghilda](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda) fixes this by placing the root in the frontier before the loop starts and yielding it when it is fetched, the same as any other page. The root is included in the output as a consequence of the architecture rather than as a special case.

## Fix

Seed `collected` with `start_url` (or its resolved URL after the first fetch) before the loop begins.

title: ragnar_find_links: return Last-Modified headers as an attribute
description:
`ragnar_find_links` already fetches every page during link discovery and has access to each page's `Last-Modified` header. Returning those timestamps as a named attribute would let callers skip re-fetching pages that have not changed since the last run, at no extra network cost.

### The problem

Incremental ingest requires knowing which pages have changed. The natural approach is to HEAD each URL for its `Last-Modified` header before deciding whether to re-fetch and re-embed. But `ragnar_find_links` already performed a full GET of every page to discover links. The modification time was available at that point and is now gone, so the caller makes a second network pass to recover information the first pass already had.

### What the change would look like

**In `read_html2`:** attach the modification time before returning:

\`\`\`r
attr(out, "last_modified") <- curl::handle_data(handle)$modified
\`\`\`

**In `ragnar_find_links`:** collect the per-URL value each time `read_html2` succeeds, build a named vector keyed by resolved URL, and attach it to the result:

\`\`\`r
attr(out, "last_modified") <- last_modified  # named POSIXct vector, url -> timestamp
\`\`\`

The return type stays a character vector. Existing callers that ignore attributes are unaffected. This follows the existing pattern: `ragnar_find_links` already returns a `problems` attribute using the same mechanism.

### Where it helps

This is only useful on hosting platforms that set `Last-Modified` to reflect the object's actual modification time. Verified behaviour:

- **S3-hosted sites** (including CloudFront distributions backed by S3): S3 sets `Last-Modified` to the object's upload time and serves it reliably. `docs.posit.co` is one example; HEAD requests return values that differ page by page and match the cadence of documentation releases.
- **GitHub Pages**: serves `Last-Modified`, reflecting the build time.
- **Netlify**: does not serve `Last-Modified`; uses ETags instead. `quarto.org` is hosted on Netlify and omits the header.

The header is a property of the hosting platform, not the static site generator. For callers targeting platforms that omit it, the attribute values are `NA` and the caller ignores them.

### Implementation notes

The relevant source is in two functions:

1. `read_html2` (internal): already attaches `attr(out, "resolved_url")` from `curl::handle_data(handle)$url`. Attaching `attr(out, "last_modified") <- curl::handle_data(handle)$modified` is a one-line addition in the same place, before `on.exit` fires and the connection closes.

2. `ragnar_find_links`: the `while` loop calls `read_html2(item$url)` and assigns the result to `page`. At that point `attr(page, "last_modified")` holds the timestamp. Collect it into a named vector keyed by resolved URL alongside the existing `resolved[item$url] <- resolved_url` line. After the loop, attach the vector as `attr(out, "last_modified")` before returning.

`curl::handle_data(handle)$modified` returns `NULL` if the server did not send the header and a `POSIXct` if it did. Normalise `NULL` to `NA_POSIXct_` before collecting so the returned vector has no gaps.

title: ragnar_retrieve_vss() OOM-kills R on large stores: missing preserve_insertion_order = false
description:
Two settings are missing from ragnar's store connection that, together, cause R to be silently killed by the OS OOM-killer on stores with ~18k chunks at 1024-dimensional embeddings. Both have single-line fixes.

### `preserve_insertion_order = false` must be set to get a streaming top-N plan

DuckDB can execute `ORDER BY metric_value DESC LIMIT k` as a streaming top-N: it maintains a fixed-size heap and never materialises more than `k` rows. This only activates when `preserve_insertion_order = false` is set on the connection. With the default (`true`), DuckDB uses a materialise-then-sort strategy instead.

For 18k rows × 1024 floats × 4 bytes, that means materialising roughly 3.7 GB inside DuckDB's allocator before the sort can run. On a typical Posit Connect server this OOM-kills the R process.

The fix is one line, applied when opening the store connection:

```r
DBI::dbExecute(store@con, "SET preserve_insertion_order = false;")
```

### No `memory_limit` means OOM kills are silent

Without a DuckDB memory ceiling, the OS OOM-killer terminates the R process with no error message or traceback. Setting a limit causes DuckDB to raise a catchable R error instead:

```r
DBI::dbExecute(store@con, "SET memory_limit = '4GB';")
```

The right value depends on the deployment, but any ceiling converts an undiagnosable crash into a recoverable error.

### Workaround

I replaced `ragnar_retrieve_vss()` with a two-stage query that avoids joining the `chunks` view. Joining `chunks` duplicates the 1024-float embedding column in the join output, which forces DuckDB to load all embedding arrays into memory regardless of the streaming plan. Text is extracted by slicing the full document string instead:

```sql
WITH top_candidates AS (
  SELECT doc_id, chunk_id, guide,
    array_cosine_similarity(embedding, <vec>) AS metric_value
  FROM embeddings
  ORDER BY metric_value DESC
  LIMIT <n_candidates>           -- n_candidates = top_k * 20
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    t.guide, d.origin, t.doc_id, t.chunk_id, t.metric_value,
    e.start AS chunk_start, e."end" AS chunk_end,
    d.text AS doc_text,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.guide ORDER BY t.metric_value DESC) AS rank_num
  FROM top_candidates t
  JOIN embeddings e USING (doc_id, chunk_id)
  JOIN documents d USING (doc_id)   -- chunks deliberately not joined
)
SELECT guide, origin, doc_id, chunk_id, metric_value,
  doc_text[chunk_start:chunk_end] AS text
FROM ranked
WHERE rank_num <= <top_k>
  AND metric_value >= <threshold>
ORDER BY metric_value DESC
```

With `preserve_insertion_order = false` and this query, retrieval takes 0.2--0.6s on an 18k-chunk store with no OOM risk.

### Suggested fix

- Set `preserve_insertion_order = false` on the connection when opening a ragnar store. There is no correctness reason to preserve insertion order when ranking by similarity score, so this is safe as a default.
- Document `memory_limit` as a recommended setting for production deployments, or apply a default.
- Optionally adopt the two-stage query to avoid the `chunks` join.

### Environment

- ragnar 0.3.1.9000
- DuckDB with duckdb-vss extension
- ~18k chunks, 1024-dimensional embeddings (Amazon Titan `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`)
- Posit Connect

title: ragnar_find_links() re-fetches duplicate URLs, making depth >= 2 extremely slow
description:
`ragnar_find_links()` with `depth >= 2` is unusably slow on any site with cross-links between pages. On `https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/` at `depth = 2` it takes over 1,000 seconds. The fixed code takes 30 seconds.

## The bug

The crawl loop checks `visited` (pages already fetched) before enqueuing child links, but not whether a URL is already waiting in the queue. Every depth-1 page that links to the same depth-2 page adds it to the queue again. On a documentation site where the navigation sidebar appears on every page, this causes every depth-2 URL to be enqueued once per depth-1 page that links to it.

On `server-pro/admin/` this inflates the queue from ~400 unique URLs to ~20,000 entries, each triggering a real HTTP request.

```r
# If depth still supports, we add items to the deque if they are not yet visited.
if (item$depth + 1 <= depth) {
  for (link in links) {
    if (!visited$`__contains__`(link)) {   # <-- only checks visited, not queued
      deque$append(list(url = link, depth = item$depth + 1))
    }
  }
}
```

## The fix

Add a `queued` set that tracks URLs the moment they enter the deque, and check it alongside `visited`:

```r
if (!visited$`__contains__`(link) && !queued$`__contains__`(link)) {
  deque$append(list(url = link, depth = item$depth + 1))
  queued$add(link)
}
```

## Benchmark

URL: `https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/`, `children_only = TRUE`

| depth | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1,005s | 30s | 33x |
| 3 | would not terminate | 28s | |

Link counts are identical before and after.

title: ragnar_store_ingest() skips re-embedding pages whose content has changed
description:
When you run `ragnar_store_ingest()` a second time to update an existing store, pages whose content has changed are re-fetched and re-chunked but **not** re-embedded. The store ends up with updated chunks but stale embeddings from the previous run.

## How it breaks

`prepare_ingest_paths()` classifies every URL as either new (`is_new_origin = TRUE`) or already known (`is_new_origin = FALSE`). That flag is passed through to `do_ingest_remote_work()` as `embed`, which skips `do_embed()` for any URL already in the store, regardless of whether the content has changed.

```r
# prepare_ingest_paths() in ingest.R
SELECT p.origin, d.origin IS NULL AS is_new_origin
FROM paths_to_ingest p
LEFT JOIN documents d USING(origin)
```

```r
# do_ingest_remote_work() in ingest.R
if (embed) {
  chunks <- do_embed(store, chunks)   # skipped when is_new_origin = FALSE
}
```

`ragnar_store_update_v2()` then writes the new chunks without embeddings, overwriting the previously correct embeddings with empty ones.

## Expected behaviour

Re-embedding should be triggered by content change, not by whether the URL is new. A page that has not changed since the last ingest should skip embedding. A page that has changed should re-embed.

## Suggested fix

Add a `content_hash` column to the `documents` table. On each ingest run, compare the hash of the newly fetched content against the stored value. Pass `embed = TRUE` when the hashes differ, `embed = FALSE` when they match. This correctly handles three cases:

- New URL: embed
- Known URL, content changed: embed
- Known URL, content unchanged: skip

title: Ragnar's `first()`/`last()` implementations error unhelpfully on empty input
description:
Ragnar defines its own `first()` and `last()` functions in [`aaa-utils.R`](https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar/blob/64acffa1ec78c32d8ceff54b5d340bf55d7a968c/R/aaa-utils.R#L43). If I am not wrong, this `first()` is only used in [`chunks_deoverlap()`'s `summarize()`](https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar/blob/64acffa1ec78c32d8ceff54b5d340bf55d7a968c/R/retrieve.R#L576). `last()` is used in that said `summarize()` and in three more places:

* <https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar/blob/64acffa1ec78c32d8ceff54b5d340bf55d7a968c/R/markdown-segment.R#L104>
* <https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar/blob/64acffa1ec78c32d8ceff54b5d340bf55d7a968c/R/markdown-chunk.R#L329>
* <https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar/blob/64acffa1ec78c32d8ceff54b5d340bf55d7a968c/tests/testthat/test-frame.R#L118>

Both, `first()` and `last()`, error in case of an empty input. Specifically, I found them to error unhelpfully if the `chunks` input of `chunks_deoverlap()` is empty (which can happen, for example when all chunks are filtered out). Being consistent (with the code base and tidyverse principles) it would be better to return an empty `deoverlapped` tibble - which we could get for example when using `dplyr::first()`. dplyr is already a dependency of ragnar.

```{r}
tibble::tibble(a = integer(), b = integer(), grp = integer()) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = grp, a = dplyr::first(a))
```

```r
ragnar_first <- function(x) x[[1L]]
ragnar_last <- function(x) x[[length(x)]]

tibble::tibble(a = integer(), b = integer()) |>
  dplyr::summarise(a = ragnar_first(a))

integer()[[1]]
integer(0) |> ragnar_last()
```

title: Support for Cognee as an external memory/GraphRAG backend
description:
I’ve been following the recent progress on ragnar and love the focus on tidy, transparent RAG workflows. I’d like to suggest an integration with [cognee](https://docs.cognee.ai/), an open-source framework that implements "AI Memory" by combining vector search with knowledge graphs.

Cognee would add a powerful GraphRAG capability. It doesn't just store chunks; it extracts entities and relationships, allowing for more complex reasoning (e.g., "how are these two concepts related?") that goes beyond simple semantic similarity.

Proposed Workflow
I think the cognee setup should be handled by the user seperatly, but ragnar could provide the "connectors" to make it feel like a native part of the R workflow.

Initialisation
ragnar_store_connect_cognee()

The integration could follow the core cognee operations:
ragnar_store_ingest_cognee() -> calls cognee.add -> cognee.cognify

ragnar_retrieve_cognee() -> calls cognee.search

Benefits to ragnar
Graph-Aware Retrieval: Moves beyond "top-k chunks" to "linked entities."

Interoperability: Users can "bring their own" cognee setup (running in Python/Docker) and use ragnar as the R interface for building and querying it.

I would be Happy to help if you’re curious to explore it further!

title: Rename store versions
description:
Currently, ragnar distinguishes between store variants using numeric versions (`version = 1` and `version = 2`). This creates the impression that `version = 1` is outdated or superseded, which is not the case.

Store `version = 1` remains relevant, particularly for use cases where chunks do not overlap. To avoid this confusion, we should rename the stores to `"simple"` and `"enhanced"`, making it clear that `version = 1` (i.e., `"simple"`) is still a valid option.

An alternative name for `"simple"` could be `"flat"`.

It’s an R interface to [ChromaDB](https://www.trychroma.com/), a lightweight vector database for storing and querying text embeddings. It might be relevant if you’re considering pluggable or scalable backends for document retrieval.

Not sure if you’re planning to support external vector stores, but just wanted to surface it in case it’s helpful — either as a possible integration or just an alternative for folks who are working with ChromaDB already.

Happy to help if you’re curious to explore it further!
Thanks again for sharing this package — excited to see where it goes!
